correct_answers.text: Cones are concentrated in the central retinal area called the macula

wrong_answers.text: Cones are located mainly in the periphery of the retina

question: Which statements accurately describe the role of rods in night vision and peripheral sight?

wrong_answers.text: Rods are concentrated in the fovea at the center of the macula

question: Which statements correctly describe how light is processed from entry into the eye to the creation of a mental image?

wrong_answers.text: Light enters the eye through the pupil before passing through the cornea

question: Which of the following statements accurately describe scotopic vision?

correct_answers.text: Occurs during nighttime, partial moonlight, or low intensity artificial illumination conditions.
Central vision (foveal cones) becomes ineffective to maintain visual acuity and color perception.
Peripheral vision (off center scanning) provides the only means of seeing very dim objects in the dark.

wrong_answers.text: Relies on central vision (foveal cones) to perceive and interpret sharp images and color.
Occurs during daytime or high-intensity artificial illumination conditions.
Occurs at dawn, dusk, or under full moonlight levels.
Requires a combination of central (foveal cones) and peripheral (rods) vision.
Is characterized by increasing visual acuity in low light.
Is primarily responsible for sharp image and color perception.
Involves foveal cones becoming more sensitive to light.
Is also known as mesopic vision.

source: Airplane Flying Handbook (FAA-H-8083-3C) Chapter 11: Night Operations Introduction

question: According to the provided text, which of the following statements accurately describe aspects of night illusions or their effects?

correct_answers.text: Visual illusions are especially hazardous.
False horizon is an illusion that leads to spatial disorientation.
Autokinesis is an illusion that leads to spatial disorientation.

wrong_answers.text: Pilots primarily rely on their vestibular system for correct information.
Bright daylight conditions increase pilot susceptibility to error.
False horizon primarily concerns the vestibular system.
Autokinesis is an illusion related to rapid acceleration.
Spatial disorientation is only caused by inner ear issues.
Visual illusions are less of a concern during night operations.
The text identifies the leans as a common night illusion.
Pilots can easily overcome visual illusions with minimal training.

question: What factors can create a false horizon during night flying?

correct_answers.text: Geometric patterns of ground lights
Aurora borealis display

question: Which of the following statements accurately describe the autokinesis phenomenon and its dangers to pilots?

correct_answers.text: A stationary light in the dark appears to move when stared at for several seconds

wrong_answers.text: Autokinesis causes a pilot to perceive the horizon as tilted during night flight
Autokinesis only occurs when multiple light sources are present in the visual field
The illusion of movement from autokinesis is caused by actual atmospheric light refraction
Autokinesis is most dangerous during daylight operations with reduced visibility
A pilot experiencing autokinesis will always correctly identify the light as stationary
Autokinesis results from the inner ear sending false motion signals to the brain
Staring at a moving light source for several seconds causes it to appear stationary
Autokinesis can be prevented by increasing cockpit lighting to maximum brightness

source: AFH Chapter 11: Night Operations Introduction, Section: Autokinesis

question: What are effective strategies to counteract the featureless terrain illusion during a night approach?

wrong_answers.text: Ignore runway lights and focus on peripheral cues

wrong_answers.text: Runway lights always make the runway appear further away

question: What are some methods to prevent landing errors due to optical illusions during night operations?

wrong_answers.text: Rely solely on visual cues without electronic aids.

Assume no increased risk during emergency distractions.

Turn off all electrical switches immediately to prevent fire.
Attempt to restart the engine only after establishing radio contact.
Initiate a steep, power-off spiral descent to conserve altitude.
Assume landing lights are unusable and prepare for a completely dark landing.
